requirement:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Stops the generator and analyzer from crashing when a [MessagePackObject] type has a member whose type is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly. It makes two changes in TypeCollector. First, the MemberNeedsKey diagnostic is now built with `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()` instead of `[0]`. Second, every diagnostic the analyzer reports now goes through a new filter that drops any diagnostic whose location is not in the current compilation. Another call site was moved into a new helper, `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation`, but that helper still indexes `[0]`. Three tests compile a library to a metadata-only image and check two things: no diagnostics, and that a resolver is generated. README and the MsgPack004 doc gained notes about types from referenced assemblies.
story.why: Metadata symbols have an empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences. Indexing `[0]` while building a diagnostic throws, and the generator then silently produces no resolver. The MemberNeedsKey path at line 1076-1077 builds its diagnostic before the accessibility check, so it runs even for a type's private fields (likely compiler-generated backing fields). That makes it the most likely culprit.
touches_beyond_requirement: A global diagnostic filter (line 239, 1444-1450) suppresses every analyzer diagnostic without an in-compilation source location. This includes diagnostics on source types that were created with a null location. That is a behavior change beyond fixing the crash.
README.md and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md gained new user-facing documentation.
The line 985 call site moved into a helper whose doc comment says it returns null for metadata. It does not: it still indexes [0].
story.confidence_overview: Medium. The FirstOrDefault change at 1077 plus the filter plausibly fixes the repro, and the tests mirror the issue's repro. I cannot see line ~735 that the issue names, so I cannot confirm every [0] path is covered. The line 985 path is still crashable. The wide filter may hide diagnostics that were previously reported for source types.

claims.text: The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull call site now calls the new GetPropertyIdentifierLocation helper. The helper is behaviorally identical to the old inline code: it still casts and indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0], so this path is NOT made safe for metadata symbols, despite what its doc comment says.
claims.requirement_quote: Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly

claims.text: The added usings (Microsoft.CodeAnalysis, Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Testing) support the MetadataReference, Compilation and ReferenceAssemblies/TestBehaviors types used by the new test helpers.
README gains a section stating that closed generics from referenced assemblies are supported and that member diagnostics for them are reported by the defining assembly.
The MsgPack004 doc gains a section stating the analyzer reports only on members declared in the compiled project.

When the analyzer supplies a report callback, TypeCollector wraps it so every diagnostic passes through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation. When no callback is supplied (generator path), reportDiagnostic stays null.
claims.requirement_quote: so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax.

claims.text: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation forwards a diagnostic only if its location is in source and its SourceTree belongs to the current compilation. Otherwise the diagnostic is silently dropped, including diagnostics created with a null location (Location.None).
claims.requirement_quote: so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax.

claims.text: The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic location now uses DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?, so building it for a metadata member (empty references) yields a null location instead of throwing IndexOutOfRangeException.
claims.requirement_quote: Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()`

claims.text: Test ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference covers a plain generic struct MyGenericStruct<T> with a keyed T member. The struct is compiled into a separate metadata-only assembly and used as MyGenericStruct<int> from a [MessagePackObject] class, with an explicit resolver.

Test ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference reproduces the issue's exact Lib/App repro: a record struct Item<T> in a referenced assembly, used as Item<int> from record Cmd. It runs with LanguageVersion.Latest.
claims.requirement_quote: So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**.

claims.text: Test ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember checks that a referenced generic struct with a public unkeyed member produces no diagnostic in the consuming project. This exercises the C2 filter dropping MemberNeedsKey for metadata members.
claims.requirement_quote:
Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

claims.text: RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync checks the requirement in two ways. First, it runs the source-generator verifier (with analyzers) and expects no diagnostics, so AD0001/CS8785 would fail it. Second, it runs the generator driver directly and asserts that no warnings are reported and that the expected resolver hint name was generated. The second check guards against the 'no generated resolver' symptom.
claims.requirement_quote: A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

claims.text: CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync and CreateCompilation emit the defining source to an in-memory image and wrap it with MetadataReference.CreateFromImage. The referenced type therefore has no syntax in the consuming compilation. Emit failure throws.
claims.requirement_quote: Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.

refusals.what: The doc comment on GetPropertyIdentifierLocation claims null is returned for metadata properties, but the code still indexes [0].
refusals.why: Misleading documentation suggests a crash path was fixed when it was not.

refusals.what: User-facing documentation was added to README and MsgPack004.md that the requirement does not ask for.
refusals.why: These are changes beyond the requirement that document new analyzer semantics.

findings.description: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation is documented as returning null for metadata properties, but it still does `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` and a hard cast. The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path (line 985) will still throw IndexOutOfRangeException for a metadata member whose key value is null. It can also throw InvalidCastException for positional record parameters. One of the three crash sites the issue names is therefore not fixed.

The filter drops every diagnostic whose Location is not in source, including diagnostics for types declared in the current compilation that were created with a null location. For example, helpers like GetParameterListLocation/GetIdentifierLocation can return null. Previously reported analyzer diagnostics may now be silently suppressed. No test covers that this does not happen.

The issue names a third `[0]` site (around original line 735) that is not in this diff. I cannot see whether it is still reachable for metadata symbols, for example on other member shapes or for classes. The tests cover only two struct shapes.

out_of_scope.description: New documentation section about referenced-assembly generics and where their diagnostics are reported. The requirement does not ask for it.
New documentation about the analyzer reporting only on members of the compiled project. It documents the new filtering behavior.
A global diagnostic filter (ReportIfLocatedInCompilation) applied to all analyzer diagnostics, which is broader than replacing the [0] indexing.
